newsitem.title: COMOROS: Patience running out for unpaid Comoro Islanders.
newsitem.headline: Patience running out for unpaid Comoro Islanders.

text.p: Several hundred Comoro Island civil servants on Thursday staged street protests and burned an effigy of President Mohamed Taki to campaign for payment of salary arrears.
Some civil servants are owed up to 12 months' wages. They burned an effigy of the president and symbolically buried it in a football ground in the capital Moroni.

"The civil servants have today shown to the government that they are determined to stand up for their rights," Ibouroi Ali Toibibou, secretary-general of the main trades union body, told the angry but peaceful crowd gathered in Moroni's Independence Square.
It was the largest protest to date by civil servants on the Indian Ocean archipelago which has a population of only about 600,000.
But the workers decided to suspend further action until after the holy Moslem month of Ramadan, due to start later on Thursday or on Friday.
The unions had given Taki's government until the end of December to pay civil servants their salary arrears or face nation-wide unrest.
But the civil servants are still unpaid with the government blaming the disastrous state of public finances.
Taki appointed a new 11-member government under Prime Minister Ahmed Abdou early this month, four weeks after general elections boycotted by the opposition.
It is Taki's third government since he was elected president last March.
The Comoro Islands have suffered up to 17 coups or attempted coups since independence from France in 1975.
